newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police arrest five for TV attack.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police arrest five for TV attack.

text.p: Turkish police have arrested five people for involvement in an attack on a private television station last week, Interior Minister Meral Aksener said on Tuesday.
"Five of those who attacked Flash TV have been caught, together with two guns," Aksener told the state-run Anatolian news agency. "We are continuing to work on this."
A group of up to 60 men, some of them armed, attacked Flash TV's Istanbul studios on Friday.

Flash reporters, speaking on live television in an office wrecked by the attackers, said this may have been a retaliation to a recent telephone interview with organised crime boss Alaattin Cakici in which he implicated several leading figures in corruption.

Police in Istanbul told Anatolian that they had traced the five attackers after the number plate of a Mercedes used by some of the gunmen was reported. They said that the two guns found on two of the detained assailants were used in the Flash TV attack.
Police forced the channel off the air on Saturday. It was up and running again on Sunday but then Turkey's television watchdog ordered it closed for two days this week over the Cakici interview.

Organised crime and its links with state and government have been on the agenda of Turkey's parliament since a crash in November when a top policeman and a wanted gangster were killed in the same car.
A legal investigation has implicated a government MP who was also in the car and a former interior minister, who resigned following the crash.
A parliamentary report painted a picture of organised crime at times working hand-in-hand with politicians and security forces.
